why: The answer applies an everyday, wrong model of StdIn: it calls StdIn a variable holding all the numbers like an array, not a stream that each read consumes once. It makes no correct prediction for any of the three inputs.

concepts.quote: StdIn is a variable that holds all the numbers, like an array.
concepts.why: StdIn is a library class of static methods that read the next token from the input stream, not a variable that stores the values.

concepts.quote: a variable that holds all the numbers, like an array
concepts.why: This assumes one variable holds many values at once, which is the multi-value variable misconception.
